question: Should OpenClaw officially support replaying trusted local edits into an updated installed package, or should the product stop at preserving a recovery bundle?
rationale: Code review can establish that the implementation is defensive, but it cannot authorize a new long-term compatibility and security contract for modified installed executables.

options.title: Preserve without replay
options.body: Keep automatic recovery bundles and diagnostics while removing executable replay, giving users a safe escape hatch without making modified installs a supported runtime state.

options.title: Preserve and opt-in replay
options.body: Accept the full recovery and explicit trusted-replay contract, including its continuing package-integrity, legacy-version, and filesystem-hardening maintenance burden.

options.title: Keep modified installs unsupported
options.body: Decline both preservation and replay and direct users toward clean reinstalls or source checkouts for maintained customizations.

recommendation.title: Preserve without replay
recommendation.body: Keep automatic recovery bundles and diagnostics while removing executable replay, giving users a safe escape hatch without making modified installs a supported runtime state.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans update behavior, release packaging, compatibility policy, and the installed-code trust boundary, matching the strongest available routing signal.
